review.notes:
2. Purpose and audience: GRTS AI (by Gratis AI) is a private AI chat assistant that runs open-source language models entirely on the device. It is for anyone who wants an AI assistant without an account, subscription or sending conversations to a server: privacy-conscious people, students, people who are often offline. Free, no ads, no in-app purchases, no account.

3. Setup: no login needed. Launch GRTS AI, tap Get Started and answer two or three short questions. To review image questions answer "Yes, sometimes" to "Will you show it photos?". The next screen recommends a model that fits the device and states its download size, expected reply speed, that it runs entirely on the device and that speed depends on the device's hardware and the model's size. Tap Download (about 0.6 to 2 GB depending on the choice, Wi-Fi recommended). Then type a question; the answer is generated on the device. Once a model is downloaded, chatting works in Airplane Mode (voice input needs its own one-time download).

4. Network activity (all of it): only Hugging Face. huggingface.co API: the list of recommended models, when the model picker opens. huggingface.co/<repo>/resolve/... over HTTPS (redirects to Hugging Face's CDN): model and vision-projector downloads (HEAD for size/checksum, Range requests to resume, one 32 MB Range request to estimate download speed), plus the optional voice-input model if the user turns on voice input. No backend of ours, no third-party AI, no cloud inference, no analytics, crash reporting or tracking. Prompts, chat history and photos never leave the device, and neither does generated text unless the user chooses to share it: llama.cpp runs inside the app and is reached only on 127.0.0.1 with a per-launch key. Replies cannot load remote images. "Report" on an answer opens the Mail app with a draft containing that answer; nothing is sent unless the user sends it.

5. Take Photo (the reported crash): build 0.55.0 had no camera usage description, so Take Photo in the paperclip menu terminated the app. Fixed: the system prompt now explains "Take a photo to ask the on-device assistant about it. Photos stay on this device." Allow: the photo is attached and the model answers about it. Don't Allow or restricted: iOS shows its black camera view with Cancel, the app explains how to turn access on in Settings, and Photo Library still works. Cancel returns to the chat. A vision load that runs out of memory now falls back to text-only instead of closing the app. Tested on iPhone X (iOS 16).

6. On-device AI and speed: three visible steps: Downloading (percent, MB, time left, Cancel), Getting your model ready (loading into memory, Stop loading) and the reply ("Reading your message...", then the text streams, Stop button). All inference runs off the main thread; the UI stays responsive. Speed depends on the hardware and model size: iPhone X (A11, CPU) with Qwen 3.5 0.8B writes about 13 tokens per second with the first words after about 5 s; a photo question takes about a minute there. A14 and newer use the GPU and are faster. The very first model start after installing can take up to about 30 s once while iOS prepares GPU shaders.

7. Regions and languages: the same everywhere; 11 interface languages following the device language. Not offered in mainland China.

8. Third-party material: the models are open-weight models published on Hugging Face by their authors, used under their public licences (Apache 2.0, LFM Open License, Gemma Terms of Use); models under non-standard licences are flagged in the picker. Answers are AI-generated and may be inaccurate, which the app states.

Recorded on a MacBook Air (Apple Silicon, 8 GB, macOS 26.1) with build 0.55.0 (5502), development-signed so it runs outside the store (same code, sandbox and entitlements): a chat with an unsent draft, closing the main window with the red button, reopening it with Window > Show Gratis AI, closing it with Cmd-W and reopening it the same way, repeating both, reopening from the Dock icon, and quitting with Quit Gratis AI. The same window comes back every time with the chat and the draft intact.
MAC_OS.notes:
2. Purpose and audience: Gratis AI is a private AI chat assistant that runs open-source language models entirely on the device. It is for anyone who wants an AI assistant without an account, subscription or sending their conversations to a server: privacy-conscious people, students, and people who are often offline (travel, flights, poor coverage). The problem it solves: mainstream AI chat apps need an account and an internet connection and process every message in the cloud. Here nothing leaves the device and it keeps working offline. The app is free, has no ads, no in-app purchases and no account.

3. Setup on the Mac: no login or credentials needed. Launch Gratis AI; it checks the Mac and recommends a model. Click Get Started, answer two short questions, then click Download. The model downloads once (its size is shown first: about 2.2 GB on an 8 GB Mac, with a 963 MB alternative offered), so please review on a fast connection. Then type a question and press Return; the answer is generated on the Mac. Main features: chat (with conversation history in the sidebar), switching models in the model picker (each shows its size and licence), image questions with a vision model (download one from the picker, attach a picture with the paperclip), language picker in the top bar, and dark mode that follows the macOS appearance. After the download everything works with Wi-Fi turned off. No sample files are needed; any image works for image questions.

Window handling (Guideline 4 fix): closing the main window with the red close button or Cmd-W keeps the app running with the chat intact. Window > Show Gratis AI in the menu bar reopens that same window (never a duplicate), and so does clicking the Gratis AI icon in the Dock. Quit Gratis AI in the app menu (Cmd-Q) quits the app.

4. External services: only Hugging Face (huggingface.co), used to download the model files once over HTTPS. There is no backend of ours, no AI cloud service, no authentication, no payment processor, no analytics or tracking. All AI processing happens on the device.

5. Regions: the app works the same in all regions. The interface is available in 11 languages and follows the system language. It is not offered in mainland China.

6. Regulation and third-party material: the app is not in a regulated industry. The AI models are third-party open-weight models published on Hugging Face by their authors and used under their public licences (Apache 2.0, LFM Open License, Gemma Terms of Use); the licence of each model is shown in the picker. We do not distribute protected third-party content. Answers are AI-generated and may be inaccurate, which the app states.
MAC_OS.review_notes: Mac: the com.apple.security.network.server entitlement is required. Vision models (e.g. Qwen 3.5 2B, SmolVLM2) run in a bundled llama.cpp llama-server helper process that the app launches and talks to over HTTP. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on a random free port, protected by a random per-launch API key; it is never reachable from other machines and accepts no outside connections. The App Sandbox blocks listening sockets, loopback included, without this entitlement, so image input would fail. To exercise it: download a vision model in the picker, attach an image in a chat and ask about it.
